title: z-index and stacking contexts
summary: Why z-index: 999 can still lose: it only competes inside its stacking context.
explanation: B has z-index: 999, yet A (3) and C (2) paint above it. B lives inside .group, which creates its own stacking context with isolation: isolate.
A stacking context is painted as one unit at its own level (here 0, since .group has no z-index). Nothing inside can rise above siblings of the group, whatever its z-index.
opacity below 1, transform, filter and position with a z-index also create stacking contexts, which is how this bites in real code.
tryThis: Delete isolation: isolate from .group: B jumps to the top.
